nodes.Name: Response
nodes.DocComment:
Response represents the response from an HTTP request.

The [Client] and [Transport] return Responses from servers once
the response headers have been received. The response body
is streamed on demand as the Body field is read.

nodes.Name: Cookies
nodes.DocComment: Cookies parses and returns the cookies set in the Set-Cookie headers.

nodes.Name: ErrNoLocation
nodes.DocComment:
ErrNoLocation is returned by the [Response.Location] method
when no Location header is present.
nodes.ValueLiteral: errors.New("http: no Location header in response")

nodes.Name: Location
nodes.DocComment:
Location returns the URL of the response's "Location" header,
if present. Relative redirects are resolved relative to
[Response.Request]. [ErrNoLocation] is returned if no
Location header is present.

nodes.Name: ReadResponse
nodes.DocComment:
ReadResponse reads and returns an HTTP response from r.
The req parameter optionally specifies the [Request] that corresponds
to this [Response]. If nil, a GET request is assumed.
Clients must call resp.Body.Close when finished reading resp.Body.
After that call, clients can inspect resp.Trailer to find key/value
pairs included in the response trailer.

nodes.Name: fixPragmaCacheControl
nodes.DocComment:
RFC 7234, section 5.4: Should treat

	Pragma: no-cache

like

	Cache-Control: no-cache

nodes.Name: ProtoAtLeast
nodes.DocComment:
ProtoAtLeast reports whether the HTTP protocol used
in the response is at least major.minor.

nodes.Name: Write
nodes.DocComment:
Write writes r to w in the HTTP/1.x server response format,
including the status line, headers, body, and optional trailer.

This method consults the following fields of the response r:

	StatusCode
	ProtoMajor
	ProtoMinor
	Request.Method
	TransferEncoding
	Trailer
	Body
	ContentLength
	Header, values for non-canonical keys will have unpredictable behavior

The Response Body is closed after it is sent.

nodes.Name: bodyIsWritable
nodes.DocComment:
bodyIsWritable reports whether the Body supports writing. The
Transport returns Writable bodies for 101 Switching Protocols
responses.
The Transport uses this method to determine whether a persistent
connection is done being managed from its perspective. Once we
return a writable response body to a user, the net/http package is
done managing that connection.

nodes.Name: isProtocolSwitch
nodes.DocComment:
isProtocolSwitch reports whether the response code and header
indicate a successful protocol upgrade response.

nodes.Name: isProtocolSwitchResponse
nodes.DocComment:
isProtocolSwitchResponse reports whether the response code and
response header indicate a successful protocol upgrade response.

nodes.Name: isProtocolSwitchHeader
nodes.DocComment:
isProtocolSwitchHeader reports whether the request or response header
is for a protocol switch.
